63-055.r: When asked: Groundnut–Andhra Pradesh, Mustard–Rajasthan, Soyabean–Madhya Pradesh, Coconut–Kerala. 2024-25 leaders: Groundnut–Gujarat, Mustard–Rajasthan, Soyabean–Maharashtra, Coconut–Tamil Nadu.

63-056.r: Largest producers: Jute → West Bengal; Tea → Assam; Rubber → Kerala; Sugarcane → Uttar Pradesh.

63-057.r: Borlaug Award → agricultural science; started 1972, named after Nobel Prize winner Norman E. Borlaug.

63-058.r: Kufri Chipsona-2 → best potato variety for processing. Kufri Chipsona-3 (2005) suits plains; Kufri Himsona suits hilly areas.

63-059.r: National Food Security Mission → raise rice, wheat and pulses output by area expansion and productivity in identified districts, sustainably; restore soil fertility, create jobs, raise farm profits.
hi: National Food Security Mission (राष्ट्रीय खाद्य सुरक्षा मिशन)

63-060.r: Crops grown mostly under subsistence farming → coarse cereals and rice.

63-061.r: Ginger → underground stem that stores food = rhizome (not bulb or corm).

63-062.r: Oatmeal → cereal grain product, eaten by people and fed to cattle as fodder.

63-063.r: Mandua (Koda) grain of Uttarakhand → exported mostly to Japan (when asked); Mandua foods are in high demand abroad.

63-064.r: Groundnut, sesame and pearl millet (bajra) → all predominantly rainfed crops of dry areas.

63-065.r: Cowpea, green gram, pigeon pea (arhar) → pulse, fodder and green manure (book: d); arhar green manure gives 40 kg nitrogen/ha. UPSC key: (a) 1 and 2.

63-066.r: Arunachal Pradesh → home to many orchid varieties; its climate suits large-scale orchid cultivation and an export-oriented orchid industry.

63-067.r: Sikkim → India's first fully organic (bio) state, declared by PM Narendra Modi in January 2016.

63-069.r: Gujarat: arid and semi-arid north, cotton grown in the central part, cash crops dominate over food crops.

63-070.r: Guar (cluster bean) → annual legume; its seed gum (guar gum) is used in hydraulic fracturing for shale gas; about 80% of world output from India and Pakistan.

63-071.r: West Bengal was India's top fish producer when asked (A true), but ~90% comes from inland waters, not the sea coast (R false). 2022-23: Andhra Pradesh leads.

63-072.r: Fish order when asked: Andhra Pradesh > Gujarat > Kerala > Tamil Nadu. 2022-23 (lakh tonnes): Andhra Pradesh 51.06, West Bengal 20.45, Karnataka 12.25, Odisha 10.52, Kerala 9.21.

63-073.r: Cotton fibre: long >5 cm (south-east USA, West Indies); medium 3.75–5 cm (Nile valley, Central Asia); short <2.5 cm (Brazil, India). Boron is a micronutrient.
63-073.c: The book prints (a) but notes the Commission's key gave (d). The edible part of apple is the fleshy thalamus, not the mesocarp, so (d) is the incorrect statement.

63-074.r: Linseed → Rabi crop (like wheat, barley, rapeseed, mustard, gram), not grown throughout the year: the wrong statement. Calcium deficiency reduces apple storage quality.

63-075.r: Lac: Jharkhand leads (2013-14), not Bihar; rice: West Bengal leads, not Andhra Pradesh → two wrong statements, no single answer (*). Also: UPAS-120 → Arhar, not gram.

63-076.r: 'Aman' rice → sown June–July, harvested November–December (not March–April). Also true: India 2nd in rice after China; soybean 20% oil, 40% protein; B.P. Pal first ICAR DG.

63-078.r: Kaushal → groundnut variety, not rice; top pulse producer → Madhya Pradesh, not Rajasthan. Two false statements; Commission accepted (d), the book gives no single answer (*).

63-079.r: All pairs wrong: Kinnaur (Himachal) is not arecanut land (Karnataka, Kerala, Assam lead); Mewat/Nuh (Haryana) not mango; Coromandel not soyabean (Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra).

63-080.r: India's share of world fruit output: 13.6% in 2014 (2nd after China, 20.9%) → nearest option 15%. Now 1st in 'other fruits n.e.c.' (FAO 2024).

63-081.r: India → largest producer of mango, banana, papaya and lemon (2020-21 report); 2nd largest fruit producer overall. So mango and papaya (2 and 4).

63-082.r: Jowar → food crop (coarse cereal), not a cash crop. Cash crops: oilseeds (groundnut, mustard), fibres (cotton, jute, mesta), plantation crops, sugarcane, tobacco.

63-083.r: Crop seasons: Sunflower → all seasons; Muskmelon → Zaid (summer); Cotton → Kharif (rainy); Linseed → Rabi (winter).
63-083.c: The printed code (b) 4 2 1 2 puts Linseed in Zaid, but the book's own match gives Linseed → Rabi (3); no option shows 4 2 1 3.

63-084.r: Water conservation in farming: reduced/zero tillage, gypsum before irrigation, leaving crop residue in the field → all keep soil moisture (1, 2 and 3).

63-085.r: Largest producers: Jute → West Bengal; Tea → Assam; Sugarcane → Uttar Pradesh; Rubber → Kerala.

63-086.r: Wrong pair: Soyabean–Andhra Pradesh (low output); soyabean leader: Madhya Pradesh when asked, Maharashtra in 2024-25. Maize now led by Madhya Pradesh; Jute–West Bengal, Cotton–Maharashtra.

63-087.r: Sultana, Gulabi and Kali Champa → grape varieties.

63-088.r: Wrong pair: Paddy–Bathua; Bathua (Chenopodium album) is a weed of wheat, pea, mustard, not paddy. Correct: Wheat–Phalaris minor, Pea–Piyazi, Berseem–Kasni.

63-089.r: Wrong pair: Paddy–Radhey; Radhey is a chickpea variety recommended for Bundelkhand (UP). Correct: Mustard–Varuna, Pea–Rachna, Linseed–Neelam.

63-090.r: Maize – Potato – Sugarcane (ratoon) – Moong → a 3-year crop rotation.

63-091.r: NABI MG → coloured wheat variety from NABI; NABI coloured wheat comes in black, blue and purple.

63-092.r: 2, 4-D → the first herbicide produced in the world.

63-093.r: Tasseling, pegging, tillering, topping → crop cultivation techniques (Maize → tasseling). Topping in gram = removing tips of young branches when the plant is 2–4 weeks old.
63-093.c: The options are misprinted (Pliny, Ptolemy, Strabo are geographers, not crops). Learn the crop stages: tasseling (maize), pegging (groundnut), tillering (wheat, rice), topping (tobacco; nipping tips in gram).

63-094.r: Mentha oil: Uttar Pradesh gave about 85% of India's output when asked; UP is the largest producer, now up to 100% per the book.

63-095.r: Wrong pair: Paddy–Wilt; wilt is not a specific paddy disease. Correct: Mustard–White rust, Bajra–Smut, Groundnut–Tikka.

63-096.r: False smut → disease of rice, not barley (the wrong statement). Correct: wheat–rust, potato–early blight, paddy–Khaira.

63-097.r: Wrong pair: Cotton–Gujarat; Maharashtra is the largest cotton producer (2024-25), Gujarat second. Rice–West Bengal, Wheat–Uttar Pradesh, Rape & Mustard–Rajasthan correct.

63-098.r: Kerala → produces both black pepper and cardamom (not Assam, J&K or Himachal).

63-099.r: Dryland (dry/rainfed) farming in India → regions with annual rainfall below 75 cm (750 mm), where rain is low and erratic.

63-100.r: APEDA → secretariat/implementing agency of NPOP; Sikkim → first fully organic state. NPOP is not under the Rural Development Ministry → statements 2 and 3.

63-101.r: Millet → food crop, not a cash crop. Cash crops are grown for sale: jute, sugarcane, peanut, coffee, cocoa, cotton, bananas.

63-102.r: Bajra: sown in hot, dry western and central India; hardy, resists dry spells; low yield in rainfed Rajasthan; Rajasthan leads production → all four true, no option fits (*).

63-103.r: Agricultural drought → low soil moisture where crops grow. Hydrological drought → low water in reservoirs; meteorological drought → degree and duration of dryness.

63-104.r: Mahi Kanchan → maize hybrid; RCB 911 → bajra hybrid. Rajasthan maize: Bhilwara, Chittorgarh, Udaipur, Banswara; bajra: western Rajasthan, Jaipur, Dausa.

63-105.r: Silviculture → art and science of cultivating forest crops: controlling establishment, growth, composition, health and quality of forests for timber, wildlife, water, recreation.

64-001.r: Stock farming → keeping and breeding livestock. Animal husbandry = scientific management of livestock: feeding, breeding, disease control.

64-002.r: Cattle density on gross cultivable land (per sq km = 100 ha): Bihar 183 (highest) > Madhya Pradesh 106 > Uttar Pradesh 77 > Haryana 25.

64-003.r: When asked: Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh (b). Cattle 2019: West Bengal 19.1 million > Uttar Pradesh 19.0 > Madhya Pradesh 18.8. Book gives no single answer (*).
64-003.c: When asked, (b) was right. The book's later figures (536.76 million livestock; cattle led by West Bengal, UP, Madhya Pradesh) are from the twentieth Livestock Census of 2019, not the '21th'.

64-004.r: When asked: cattle–MP, buffaloes–UP (a). 20th Livestock Census 2019: livestock UP, Rajasthan, MP; buffaloes UP, Rajasthan, Gujarat; sheep Telangana > Andhra Pradesh > Karnataka. UP leads milk (2024-25).

64-005.r: Jamunapari → India's highest milk-yielding goat breed.

64-006.r: Tharparkar cattle → western border districts of Rajasthan (Jaisalmer, Barmer, Jodhpur) and Kutch (Gujarat). Jaisalmer tops Rajasthan in per capita milk production.

64-007.r: Hallikar → Karnataka cattle breed, not Rajasthan. Rajasthan native cattle: Rathi, Tharparkar, Nagori. Mewati (Kesi) → Haryana breed.

64-008.r: Sahiwal → cow breed with very high milk yield (from Pakistan). Gangotri (UP) yields little; Haryana and Tharparkar are dual-purpose (draught and milk).
64-008.c: The book places Sahiwal in Sindh province; the breed comes from the Sahiwal (Montgomery) area of Punjab, Pakistan. Red Sindhi is the Sindh breed.

64-009.r: India → 1st in world milk production. 2024-25: Uttar Pradesh 1st (15.66%), Rajasthan 2nd (14.82%).

64-010.r: Uttar Pradesh → top milk producer (also in 2011-12). 2024-25: UP 15.66%, Rajasthan 14.82%, Madhya Pradesh 9.12%, Gujarat 7.78%, Maharashtra 6.71%.

64-011.r: Operation Flood → milk production and distribution; launched 1970 by NDDB under Dr. Verghese Kurien; made India the world's largest milk producer.

64-012.r: Dr. Verghese Kurien → Father of India's White Revolution (milk production), which made India the largest milk producer in the world.

64-015.r: Milk production order (book, 2024-25): Madhya Pradesh > Gujarat > Punjab > Haryana; India ranks 1st in the world.

64-016.r: Wrong pair: Sheep–Gir (Gir is not a sheep breed). Correct: Cow–Deoni, Goat–Barbari, Buffalo–Bhadawari.
64-016.c: The book's 'correct match' table repeats Sheep–Gir, contradicting its own answer; Gir is a cattle (cow) breed.

64-017.r: Kharai camels: swim long distances (often more than 3 km) in the sea to reach grazing areas; name from local word 'Khara' = saline.
64-017.c: Kharai camels live in Kutch (Gujarat), not Ladakh, so statement I is false and (d) cannot be right; the book itself doubts IV. Statements II and III hold, giving (b).
